# Assumptions and data

**All data is synthetic**, generated by `scripts/generate_orders.py` (seed 11). Plateful is fictional. Nothing here comes from any real company, employer or customer.

## Data: `data/orders.csv` (10,000 rows, one per order)
| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| order_id, created_at, city, customer_id, restaurant_id, items, order_value | Order basics (900 customers, 60 restaurants, 6 cities, one illustrative currency) |
| promised_minutes, actual_minutes | Promised and actual delivery time (blank if cancelled) |
| status | Delivered or Cancelled |
| cancelled_by, cancel_stage, cancel_reason_code | Who cancelled, when in the order, and why (reason blank for about 18%) |
| wasted_food_cost | 60% of order value if cancelled during prep or in transit, otherwise 0 |
| refund_requested, refund_reason, refund_amount | Refund request (1/0), reason, amount requested |
| prior_refunds_90d | Customer's earlier refund requests in the previous 90 days |
| refund_decision, decision_hours | Auto-approved, Manual-approved or Manual-denied, and hours to decide |
| contact_channel, chase_contacts, agent_minutes | How the customer contacted support, repeat contacts, total agent minutes |
| refund_amount_paid | Amount paid (0 if denied) |

## Rules built into the generator
- Current policy: auto-approve when the amount is at most 10 and the customer has fewer than 3 refund requests in the past 90 days; everything else is manual.
- Late delivery (over 10 minutes) raises the refund request chance from about 1.5% to 18%.
- A small hidden group (36 of 900 customers, about 4%) orders more, requests refunds more often (25%), mostly "missing item" or "never arrived", and has a higher denial rate. The flag is not in the file, so the analysis has to find them through concentration.
- Manual decisions take a median of about 14 hours with a long tail; when over 24 hours, customers chase far more often.
- 20% of cancellations have no reason code.
- Cancellation chance rises when the delivery is badly late.

## Cost assumptions (change them in `scripts/analyse.py`)
- Support agent: 20 currency units per hour, fully loaded.
- Food lost on a cancellation after preparation starts: 60% of order value.
- Handling time per contact: chat 8 minutes, phone 12, email 10; chasing contact 6 minutes; manual review about 12 minutes.

## Limits
Synthetic patterns and noise are my design. Results are for demonstrating analysis, and real data would need its own validation.
